attributes.probed_form: PROBE 1 (real 10 -> 25, insns 50 -> 51): added `char* buf;` as the first declaration and `buf = (char*)sSpeechNameBuf;` as the first statement, ahead of `AudioKillBySound(0xC0000);`, rewriting all four consumers (two sprintf, AudioRegisterNameBanks, AudioFindSound) from `(char*)sSpeechNameBuf` to `buf`. PROBE 2 (real 25, byte-identical object): same, but as a declaration initializer -- `char* buf = (char*)sSpeechNameBuf;` with no assignment statement. PROBE 3 (real 25, byte-identical object): probe 2 wrapped in `#pragma opt_propagation off` before the function and `#pragma opt_propagation reset` after it, the scoped form this TU already uses around AudioBuildMusicName at lines 649/701.
attributes.residual: 10 real rows, ONE named mechanism. Target materialises &sSpeechNameBuf at function ENTRY, straddling the prologue: `lis r3,0 @sSpeechNameBuf(ADDR16_HA)` at +0x4 (before the `stwu`) and `addi r31,r3,0 @sSpeechNameBuf(ADDR16_LO)` at +0x14 (immediately AFTER `stmw r30,8(r1)`), giving r31 = buf and r30 = ch. Ours CSEs the same four uses into r31 correctly but materialises the pair late, at first use around +0x5c. HAZARD WORTH THE CAP, and the reason the obvious cure must not be banked: anchoring the address with an explicit local does move the materialisation to entry, but MWCC then schedules the LO `addi` into the pre-prologue gap where r30/r31 are not yet saved, so it lands in r0 (`addi r0,r3,0`) and needs a recovery `mr r30,r0` after the `stmw` -- costing one instruction, LOSING count parity 50/50 -> 51/50, and flipping the coloring to buf=r30 / ch=r31 (target is the reverse). Per probe.py's own class warning, a count-asymmetric residual is outside EVERY postprocessor class, so the 'improvement' would have traded a class-eligible baseline for a state no rule can finish. Baseline is strictly better and is what remains in the tree.
